bracket.method: a corrected prior is a probability, so it lies in [0, 1]. The supply is replayed at the SUPREMUM (every prior-mass score set to 1.0) and at the INFIMUM (the prior-mass dimension removed entirely) and both are compared against the as-flown supply on all 104. Any semantically corrected prior lies weakly between the two, so agreement at both extremes is agreement everywhere.

a2t_prior_dimension_sensitivity.defect: rails.knowledge_build_a2t sets prior_score = tool_total / category_total, counting a tool's rows across EVERY domain against a single (domain, category) denominator. The numerator is not a subset of the denominator, so the ratio is not a conditional probability and has no reason to be <= 1. The intended quantity is p(tool | domain, category) = count(tool AND category) / count(category). The landed max(1.0, sup) repair in kb_policy._dimension_scales is a monotone rescale of a wrong ratio, not a correction of it.
a2t_prior_dimension_sensitivity.disclosure: Q1's case-(b) membership and Q2's reachability curve are RANKING statements. They were computed under the as-flown, defective prior and are the record of what actually happened. The bracket above states, as a measurement rather than an assumption, whether any correction of that prior could move them.

k3_dispatch_projection.dispatch_predicate: a2t_label_normalizer returns None -- the answer did not parse, carried no calls, or its PRIMARY tool name is outside the 151-entry label vocabulary. K3's form constraint removes the first two causes and leaves the third.
k3_dispatch_projection.e_c_precedent: the rejected E-C variant forced label recovery on every sample and took evidence contacts to zero (projected 54-67/100 against 72). The plan admits K3 only because it leaves out-of-vocabulary answers out-of-vocabulary; that carve-out is measured here rather than assumed.

flown_dispatch_composition.reading: only the third class survives a pure FORM constraint; the first two are exactly what a role constraint is designed to remove, and removing them removes the trajectory from the reachable set

projection_upper_bound_on_repair.label: UPPER bound on form repair (BLEND arm's own final answers, evidence in context) -> LOWER bound on surviving dispatch

admissibility.any_depth_change_is_a_knob_change: k, m, tau, c and top_l are all cells of configs/policy/kb-policy-v1-dev100.json, which is LOCKED. No depth in this curve is admissible without an owner knob decision; this module computes the curve and makes no such decision.
admissibility.k_widen_prior: K-WIDEN K1 FLOWN plus its offline width-5 replay: widening the retrieval window changed the supply on 32 of 100 trajectories and produced 0 width-attributable flips (71/100 at delta -1). A reachability curve is evidence about REACHABILITY only; K-WIDEN is the measured counter-example to treating depth as conversion.

binding_stage.semantics: a facet whose best cosine is below tau = 0.65 is refused by the percept gate at EVERY window depth, so for those trajectories no value of k or m is a fix at all. A facet that passes tau but whose TARGET is outside the top_l = 3 target budget is refused by the budget, not by the window -- widening k or m cannot reach it either.

q2_reachability_curve.question: for the case-(b) trajectories whose gold value exists in the KB, what is its rank under the CURRENT post-repair ranker and how deep would the admitted window have to go to reach it?

largest_cluster_supply.reading: one key, one supply. Every trajectory in this cluster received the SAME targets whatever its utterance was about, so gold can only arrive by coincidence -- when the trajectory's own gold tool happens to be one of the constant targets.

query_key_degeneracy.provenance: the content-dimension query vector is the embedding of the trajectory's OWN contact-0 answer text -- contact 0's output IS the retrieval key. Verified in this row by re-hashing each landed Pass-A text against the text_sha256 its own landed query-vector record carries (ccd.load_a2t_attempt4).
query_key_degeneracy.question: does the retrieval key carry trajectory-specific information on the dead-direct subgroup at all?
query_key_degeneracy.reading: a distinct-query-vector count below the trajectory count means several trajectories share ONE retrieval key and therefore ONE recalled facet set, whatever their utterances were about

ranker_ordering_check.consequence: with one dimension per content facet and zero prior mass the registered ranker's score is an affine map of the cosine, so the content-facet ordering IS the cosine ordering and every depth statement below is a statement about that single ordering

recall_fidelity.semantics: the vectorised full-KB cosine sweep is not trusted until kb.multidim_recall admits the same facet set with the same scores on the probed samples and kb_policy._cosine reproduces each probed cosine to 1e-9
